summary: Unapplied virtual-card authorizations preventing pending payrun
description: Issue summary: Several virtual-card authorizations created in the last scheduled payrun window were not applied to their matching invoices, leaving holds open and preventing the payrun from completing. Impact: Current weekly payrun (Mar 11 cutoff) is stuck in Pending Funds due to ~12 vendor card holds totaling $48,312. This blocks settlement and will push reconciliation into next cycle if not resolved. Observed behavior: authorization exists in payments ledger but system mark-as-captured step does not find corresponding invoice lines when authorizations were split across multiple PO line items with different currency rounding behavior. Expected behavior: authorizations should be matched and applied to invoice captures (partial or aggregated) so holds clear and payrun can proceed. Attachments: payment_ledger_export, sample_authorizations.csv, screenshot_payrun_queue.png. Links: Slack thread #finance-ops: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0FINOPS/p163, Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/FIN/Virtual+Card+Reconciliation
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a PO with multiple line items scoped in USD where one line item has VAT and one does not
2) Issue a virtual-card authorization that covers the combined total, but the payment provider splits the authorization into two tokens (merchant side) due to descriptor limits
3) Upload invoice that maps each authorization token to different PO lines with minor cent-level rounding differences
4) Run reconciliation job (recon-v2) used by payrun scheduler
5) Observe that reconciler does not apply either authorization to the invoice capture and leaves holds open.

comments: Aisha Patel (Reporter) - 2026-03-10: Created ticket after noticing pending payrun; attached sample CSV and ledger extract.
Finance Ops (Emma Rodriguez) - 2026-03-10: Assigned to payments eng and reconciliation. Reached out to vendor (CardProvider) to request token mapping table for split auths.

Payments Eng (Liam Chen) - 2026-03-11: Initial triage: reconciler currently only matches by exact authorization token -> invoice.map.auth_token. If provider splits at merchant side into mt tokens, we need aggregation by external_merchant_id + po_reference. Opened PR to add aggregation hint.
SRE (Nina Kaur) - 2026-03-11: Observed increased latency on recon-v2 job but not related errors. Will monitor after code change.
Finance Ops (Emma Rodriguez) - 2026-03-12: Temporary workaround applied: Finance released 6 holds manually to allow partial settlement; remaining holds need reconciler fix.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Payment provider issues split authorization tokens that reference same external_merchant_id; reconciler matching logic used strict token equality and failed to aggregate. Confirmed sample where two auth tokens (mt_abc123, mt_def456) share same external_merchant_id and total amount equals invoice. Reconciler log shows 'token_split_mismatch' for these items. Payments service retains mapping of original virtual-card event with external_merchant_id and po_reference. Proposed fix: update reconciliation to perform secondary aggregation pass grouping unmatched auths by external_merchant_id + po_reference and attempt to apply aggregated amount subject to tolerance (<= $0.50). Added unit tests and plan to rollout on recon-v2-canary. Also reached out to CardProvider for absolute token mapping export and timeframe for prevention fixes.
resolution: Workaround: Finance manually released six holds and completed a partial payrun to avoid immediate disruption. Permanent fix: payments team merged PR #482 to allow aggregation-by-external-merchant_id for recon-v2 (see related PR). Deployment: recon-v2-canary deployed 2026-03-12 09:00 UTC; subsequent reconciliations matched the remaining 6 authorizations and payrun completed successfully. Postmortem action items: (1) Add aggregation tolerance config to reconciliation (owner: payments), (2) Add alert when unmatched_auth_count > 5 for scheduled payruns (owner: observability), (3) Confirm vendor tokenization behavior with CardProvider and request consistent tokenization for virtual-card flows (owner: Finance Ops). Follow-up ticket created: INT-718999 (reconciliation-config-add-tolerance).
